## Result

Propose a negative answer to Kourovka Notebook 21.60 (UnsolvedMath ID 2569): take G = SL(2,5), p = 2. All three projective indecomposable F₂G-module types satisfy the positive rational-reduction condition, while the eight-dimensional projective cannot lift because its forced ordinary character contains a quaternionic irreducible with odd multiplicity.

[Complete proof](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/c7805ab0804f50c6f4b0d1dda99e433dbb702ae2/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/2569/COUNTEREXAMPLE.md)

## Validation and limits

- Five substantive mathematical attempts are preserved.
- Exact finite checks, a contributing character/decomposition check, a separate fresh adversarial audit, and a narrow portability review passed.
- The proof is unchanged from the fresh-audited snapshot. Author, contributor, and fresh-review work are explicitly separated.
- AI-assisted candidate awaiting specialist human verification; no formal proof-assistant certification or historical priority claim.
- The qualified supplemental Ext warning is not needed for the main counterexample.

## Reproduce

In unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/2569, run:

- python verify_counterexample.py
- python verify_controls.py
- python contributor_checks/check_character_data.py
- python independent_audit/independent_audit.py

The latter two require SymPy. The public independent verifier runs from the included mathematical coefficient data and proof alone; every mathematical result matches the original audit.

## Scope

26 authored mathematics/check/review files, plus only rank 466's queue status queued → claimed_solved and turns 0/5 → 5/5. All other queue bytes and unrelated work are preserved against fresh main. No queue.py changes, source PDFs, source text, screenshots, private context, merge, or release.
title: KOU-21.60: SL(2,5) counterexample candidate (claimed_solved, 5/5)
